problem: The caption says "The figure follows the worked example", but the figure is placed before Worked Example 1. Also the "Derivatives" node shows only ∂u/∂x = 3e-3 and ∂v/∂y = 2e-3, yet the next node produces γxy = 3e-3, which needs ∂u/∂y and ∂v/∂x. Those two mixed derivatives appear nowhere in the diagram, so a student cannot see where the shear number comes from, even though the caption tells them to notice that γxy uses both mixed derivatives.
fix: Caption: "The figure previews the worked example." Derivative node should list all four: ∂u/∂x = 3e-3, ∂v/∂y = 2e-3, ∂u/∂y = 1.5e-3, ∂v/∂x = 1.5e-3, then the shear node adds the last two to give γxy = 3e-3.

problem: The sign convention for X, Y, Z is not stated. The text says only "add X to the x equation", but quiz Q5 needs X = -6 N/mm³ to restore balance. Without knowing that X is positive along +x, a student cannot tell whether the needed body force is +6 or -6.
fix: "Take X, Y, Z positive along +x, +y, +z. The equations then read ∂σx/∂x + ∂τxy/∂y + ∂τxz/∂z + X = 0, and similarly for y and z. A body force pointing along -x has a negative component."

problem: "the strain is wrong by 1000" does not say whether the answer comes out too large or too small, which is exactly the point a student needs in the exam.
fix: "If u is in mm and x is in m, ∂u/∂x comes out 1000 times too small (mm/m instead of mm/mm), so convert x to mm before differentiating; the true strain is 1000 times the unconverted value."
